advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert the call_tool result is an error payload (e.g. isError / error content) rather than only asserting the process survives.
evidence: `try: _call_read_tool(tool, **args)` followed by `except Exception:  pass` — the success/return path is unasserted
AC: 'A test asserts an MCP tool returns an error payload (not a dead server) with REBAR_ROOT unset in a non-repo cwd'
test_mcp.py:337 shows call_tool returns normally on a domain error ('# no raise'); the return value carries the error payload but is discarded here
`monkeypatch.chdir(tmp_path)  # a real dir that is NOT a git work tree` — asserted only in a comment
src/rebar/_engine_support/reads.py:132-140 runs `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` which ascends parent dirs

`_call_read_tool(tool, **args)` inside `try:` with only `except SystemExit` (fail), `except Exception: pass`, `except BaseException` (fail) — the normal (no-exception) return path has NO assertion (lines 54-66)
AC from ticket 176d: 'A test asserts an MCP tool returns an error payload (not a dead server) with REBAR_ROOT unset in a non-repo cwd' — the payload/isError side is never checked
ABSENCE: no assertion on the CallToolResult (e.g. isError True / error text) that call_tool returns; a tool silently returning success would not be caught
advisory.finding: The tests assert the server does not die (no SystemExit/BaseException) but never assert that call_tool returns an actual error payload; the AC requires 'returns an error payload (not a dead server)'. A regression where the gate tool silently succeeds or returns non-error data would pass this test.
merged_from: Neither test guards the assumption that tmp_path is outside a git worktree; tracker_dir runs `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` which walks UP the directory tree, so if the temp root sits inside a git repo the non-repo precondition would not hold and the test would silently exercise the wrong path.

The parametrized survival test never asserts the tool returned an ERROR payload; it only fails on SystemExit/BaseException. A regression where the tool returns a success payload (or never reaches the tracker_dir site) returns normally, fires no except clause, and passes — leaving the ticket AC 'returns an error payload (not a dead server)' half unverified.
advisory.suggested_fix: Capture the call_tool return value and assert it signals an error (FastMCP's (content, structured) tuple with an error/isError indication) instead of discarding it in `except Exception: pass`.

advisory.suggested_fix: For the second call, chdir into an initialized rebar repo (or set REBAR_ROOT to a real worktree) and assert a successful/error-free payload, matching the docstring.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the liveness second call a genuinely SUCCESSFUL call (build a real tracker via rebar_repo / chdir into a git worktree) and assert it returns a non-error result.
evidence: Docstring: 'first against a non-repo cwd, then against a real tracker' (lines 74-76)

ABSENCE: no assertion that the second call SUCCEEDS (returns a non-error result), so a server left able-to-fail-again but unable-to-succeed-again passes
advisory.finding: The liveness test's 'second call' does not exercise the real-tracker/successful-serve claim its docstring makes: cwd stays at the non-repo tmp_path, no tracker is built, the same failing args are reused, and the second failure is swallowed by `except Exception: pass`. It proves only that a second IDENTICAL failing call raises no BaseException — not that the server can serve a SUCCESSFUL call after a prior failure.
advisory.suggested_fix: After the first failing call, switch to a real tracker (use the rebar_repo fixture or init a git worktree + chdir) and assert the second call_tool returns a non-error CallToolResult, so the test proves the server still serves rather than merely fails-again without dying.
